candidates.summary: Russian drone attacks in the Kyiv region on November 22 killed at least nine people, according to Ukrainian officials cited in late reporting: at least five in a collapsed apartment building in Dymer, three at a grocery store in Vyshneve, and one in the Bila Tserkva district. The Dymer toll had reached five by a 10 p.m. local-time update. A seven-year-old boy was rescued alive from the building that evening after nearly 14 hours beneath the rubble. Search operations continued, repeatedly interrupted by aerial threats. These figures supersede the earlier four-death regional account.
candidates.title: Reported death toll rises in Kyiv-region attacks as child is rescued from rubble
candidates.geography: Dymer, Vyshneve and Bila Tserkva district, Kyiv region, Ukraine

candidates.summary: A failure of Delta Air Lines' automated aircraft weight-and-balance system disrupted flights nationwide on Sunday, November 22. Delta said the system was restored during the afternoon, but delays continued into the evening. The FAA briefly restricted Delta flights bound for Atlanta and said its own air-traffic systems were not responsible. Employees used manual calculations while automation was unavailable. At 9 p.m. Eastern, FlightAware data showed more than half of all flights at Atlanta's airport had experienced delays; weather also contributed to disruptions.
candidates.title: Delta restores weight-and-balance system but flight delays persist into Sunday evening
